slides.0.title: Principal White Grapes
slides.0.subtitle: Viognier, Marsanne and Roussanne
slides.1.title: Viognier: aroma and revival
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Aromatic
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Apricot, peach, white blossom and musk, with low acidity, high alcohol and an oily texture
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Near extinction
slides.1.highlights.1.content: By the mid-20th century only about a dozen hectares remained around Condrieu (accounts vary); it was abandoned as hard to grow with erratic yields
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Revival from the 1980s
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Condrieu is back to about 221 ha in 2024 (Inter Rhône); plantings spread worldwide, and the Rhône had about 1,600 ha in 2025
slides.1.highlights.3.title: Condrieu and Château-Grillet
slides.1.highlights.3.content: Both are 100% Viognier; Côte-Rôtie reds may also co-ferment a little Viognier
slides.1.content: Sources differ on the exact area at the low point, so this lesson leaves it out of the quiz.
slides.2.title: Marsanne and Roussanne: northern whites
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Marsanne
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Rich and waxy, with honey, almond and pear; moderate acidity, rounder with age
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Roussanne
slides.2.highlights.1.content: More delicate, with flowers, herbal tea and spice, higher acidity and strong ageing potential; harder to grow, about 1,200 ha (2025)
slides.2.highlights.2.title: A natural pair
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Often blended: Marsanne gives body, Roussanne perfume and acidity; they lead the whites of Hermitage, Crozes-Hermitage, Saint-Joseph and Saint-Péray
slides.2.content: The northern white default is Marsanne + Roussanne (Condrieu and Château-Grillet being the Viognier exceptions).
slides.3.title: Southern and other whites
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Grenache Blanc
slides.3.highlights.0.content: The most planted southern white (about 2,100 ha, 2025); full-bodied with lowish acidity
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Clairette, Bourboulenc and more
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Clairette (about 1,300 ha) is herbal and fresh; Bourboulenc keeps acidity; Picpoul is also permitted
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Muscat Blanc à Petits Grains
slides.3.highlights.2.content: About 1,400 ha (2025), used for Muscat de Beaumes-de-Venise and other vins doux naturels (VDN)
slides.3.highlights.3.title: White share
slides.3.highlights.3.content: White is about 13% of output (2025): small, but stylistically diverse
slides.3.content: Southern whites are mostly blends, balancing retained acidity against a rounded palate.
slides.4.title: Northern vs southern whites at a glance
slides.4.highlights.0.title: North: few grapes, small areas
slides.4.highlights.0.content: Three principal grapes: Viognier, Marsanne, Roussanne; Condrieu is pure Viognier, others mostly Marsanne + Roussanne
slides.4.highlights.1.title: South: many grapes, mostly blends
slides.4.highlights.1.content: Grenache Blanc, Clairette, Bourboulenc, Roussanne and others are blended; Châteauneuf-du-Pape and Cairanne, among others, make white
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Blind-tasting clue
slides.4.highlights.2.content: Intense apricot and white flowers with oily texture → Viognier; honeyed, waxy with moderate acidity → Marsanne-led
slides.4.content: Rule of thumb: north = few grapes, place-led; south = many grapes, blended.
